PS 10.1 | Coulomb’s Law and Charge

Problems A balloon rubbed against denim gains a charge of -8.0 µC. What is the electric force between the balloon and the denim when the two are separated by a distance of 5.0 cm? Two identical conducting spheres are placed with their centers 0.30 m apart. One is given a charge of +12 x 10-9 C and the other is given a charge of -18 x 10-9 C. Find the electric force exerted on one sphere by the other. The spheres are connected by a conducting wire. After equilibrium (of charge) is reached, find the electric force between the two spheres Two electrostatic point charges of +60.0 µC and +50.0 µC exert a repulsive force on each other of 175 N. What is the distance between the two charges? A charge of +2.00 x 10-9 C is placed at the origin, and another charge of +4.00 x 10-9 C is placed at x=1.5 m. Find the point between these two charges where a charge, q3 of +3.00 x 10-9 C should be placed such that the net electric force on q3 is zero. A charge q1 of -5.00 x 10-9 C and a charge q2 of -2.00 x 10-9 C are separated by a distance of 40.0 cm. Find the equilibrium position for a third charge of +15.0 x 10-9 C. An electron is released above the Earth’s surface. A second electron directly below it exerts just enough electric force on the first electron to cancel the gravitational force on it. The mass of an electron is 9.109 x 10-31 kg. Calculate the distance at which the electrical force cancels the gravitational force acting upon it. A proton and an electron in a hydrogen atom are separated, on average, by a distance of 5.3 x 10-11 m. What is the magnitude and direction of the electric field set up by a proton at the position of the electron? An electric field of 2.0 x 104 N/C is directed along the positive x-axis. What is the electric force on an electron in this field? What is the electric force on a proton in this field?

Answers (-) 230 N, attractive (a) 2.2 x 10-5 N, attractive (b) 9.0 x 10-7 N, repulsive 0.393 m X = 0.62 m 24.5 cm from q1 (15.5 cm from q2) 5.08 m 5.1 x 1011 N/C away from the proton (a) 3.2 x 10-15 N attractive or along the negative x-axis (b) 3.2 x 10-15 N repulsive or along the positive x-axis
